top_choice_rationale: P002 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) rests on three separable, datable building blocks: time-dependent pricing, staggered contracts with an interest-rate rule, and the welfare-based policy synthesis. The work is 25 to 40 years old and has been extended, criticised and used in policy institutions throughout. With the citation confined to nominal-rigidity theory, policy rules and the welfare framework, it makes no claim about Phillips-curve slope or forecasting, which handles the post-2008 and 2021-23 inflation concerns. Attribution is the main weakness: eight names are credited and any three-person cut omits Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets. I judge that a defensible choice of strand, not a flaw in the contribution. P001 (Helpman, Melitz) is second because its credit line is cleaner, although the uncredited Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum lineage and the functional-form dependence of the welfare gains limit it. P003 is third: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are a coherent evidential unit, but magnitude and persistence are debated and the task-framework credit sits partly outside the ballot. P004 is fourth because of partial overlap with the 2024 prize and partly observational identification. A prize on any of the four is preferable to no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile with respect to Calvo, Taylor, Woodford or the credited names on B010, B032 and B016. Disclosed, not adjudicated: SSE affiliation alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and long-standing co-authorship in matching, auctions and market design, none involving a credited candidate.
